sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Only 2 species in the genus; no key provided. A. trestus is very close to this species, the worker differing in the far more developed spines of the enteric-valve armature and slightly different mandible proportions; the only difference in the alate of A. trestus is the more evenly rounded postclypeus. This species is the most widely distributed recorded in that monograph, from Gambia in West Africa eastwards.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark brown to very dark brown or chestnut brown, sometimes darker above the ocelli; fontanelle broadly to slightly elongate oval, flat, with a median ridge or slightly raised, smaller than to clearly larger than an ocellus, orange-yellow to dark brown; central spot flat or slightly raised, oval, smaller than the fontanelle, concolorous with the head capsule or slightly paler; postclypeus yellow-brown to dark brown, labrum yellow to brown; frontal mark a flat or slightly concave crescent, clearly paler than the head capsule; antennae yellow-brown to dark brown. Pronotum brown to dark brown, mesonotum and metanotum brown, the transverse sutures dark, from weak to distinct; femora pale yellow-brown to brown, tibiae paler, tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites brown to dark brown, the dorsolateral spiracles paler than or concolorous with the tergites; sternites and ventrolateral spiracles brown, the middle of the sternites paler; cerci yellow to pale brown. Posterior margin of head capsule evenly rounded or nearly so, slightly undulate; ocelli medium-sized, the distance to the compound eye from less than half its minimum diameter to slightly more than its minimum diameter; postclypeus weakly to strongly inflated, Pcl/W 0.20—0.34, posterior margin rarely evenly rounded, mostly arched at the middle, the median suture distinct. Head pilosity yellow-brown to brown, from fine, sparse, short and slightly uneven felt with outstanding setae, to uneven and without felt. Other characters as for the genus. Measurements (mm; 24 specimens, 16 localities): width of head between compound eyes W 0.90—1.35 (1.146 ± 0.117); ocellus 0.07—0.13 × 0.10—0.17 (0.094 ± 0.014 × 0.125 ± 0.018); ocellus to compound eye 0.04—0.10 (0.063 ± 0.015); postclypeus length Pcl 0.22—0.34 (0.289 ± 0.029); antennal segment III 0.02—0.08 (0.045 ± 0.013), segment IV 0.04—0.09 (0.064 ± 0.016), segment V 0.04—0.09 (0.064 ± 0.015); left mandible apical tooth to first marginal tooth La 0.08—0.11 (0.097 ± 0.007), first to third marginal tooth Li 0.14—0.20 (0.172 ± 0.016), third marginal tooth to molar area Lm 0.06—0.10 (0.085 ± 0.013); right mandible apical tooth to first marginal tooth Ra 0.09—0.11 (0.100 ± 0.006), first to second marginal tooth Ri 0.10—0.15 (0.128 ± 0.014), second marginal tooth to molar area Rm 0.06—0.11 (0.083 ± 0.013); mesonotum width M 0.28—0.49 (0.370 ± 0.056); metanotum width N 0.29—0.50 (0.374 ± 0.056).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule yellow-white to yellow, pilosity yellow, sparse. Postclypeus weakly to moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.21—0.29, Pcl/Ri 1.89—2.71. Left mandible accessory marginal tooth about as large as the third marginal tooth, separated from the molar prominence in surface view by a wide, deep notch, composite ratio La/Li·Lm 7.90—12.75; right mandible first and second marginal teeth with equal anterior margins, Ra/Ri·Rm 10.49—15.40. Enteric-valve armature with 1—9 conspicuous spines at cushion position 3 (more than 5 in only two records), at position 4 sometimes not protruding from the valve opening and rarely with more than 1 conspicuous spine (only small spines among ten), both positions with additional larger numbers of small or minute spines; positions 1 and 2 with several small spines, or all minute. Membranous wall of the valve outside the cushions with minute spines. Other characters as for the genus. Measurements (mm): head width W 0.81—1.05 (0.934 ± 0.069); foretibia width Tw 0.09—0.14 (0.114 ± 0.010); foretibia length Ti 0.56—0.84 (0.689 ± 0.090); postclypeus length Pcl 0.19—0.33 (0.268 ± 0.032); La 0.08—0.10 (0.088 ± 0.005); Li 0.13—0.16 (0.148 ± 0.010); Lm 0.05—0.07 (0.060 ± 0.007); Ra 0.08—0.09 (0.087 ± 0.005); Ri 0.09—0.12 (0.109 ± 0.008); Rm 0.05—0.07 (0.060 ± 0.005).

note: Adapted from the species-level description in Sands (1972), original in English; this species has no soldier, only the alate and the worker; the synonyms Mirotermes (Cubitermes) natalensis Holmgren, 1913 and Mirotermes (? Procubitermes) mfolozii Fuller, 1925 are both placed as new synonyms (Syn. n.); the lectotype designation, figure numbers (Text-figs 307—310, 315—320; Pl. 2, figs 8—11) and locality records are not translated; the measurement table has two parallel columns (this species and "A. natalensis"), only the column for this species is recorded here, and the parenthetical values are Mean ± S.D.
